extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of architecture and art history; architects, conservators, and connoisseurs interested in Gothic and Renaissance palace ornament
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for assessing architecture and sculpture on the Ducal Palace—how angles, sculptural program, technique, and historical interventions convey style, purpose, and durability. Useful for analyzing Gothic vs Renaissance treatment of palace façades and sculptural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking the angle (peculiarly Gothic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: "This principle of breaking the angle is peculiarly Gothic, arising partly out of the necessity of strengthening the flanks of enormous buildings... partly out of the conditions of Gothic warfare... partly out of the natural dislike of the meagreness of effect in buildings which admitted large surfaces of wall, if the angle were entirely unrelieved."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether angles are softened/modified (buttresses, turrets, niches) to (1) provide structural reinforcement, (2) respond to defensive/functional needs, and (3) avoid visual meagreness on large wall surfaces. Examples: groups of buttresses or turrets at corners; assess whether angle treatment is integrated structurally and aesthetically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of main decoration on angles
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Ducal Palace...throws the main decoration upon its angles."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the building emphasizes corner articulation as principal loci for sculpture and ornament; check how decorative emphasis at corners establishes visual hierarchy for a near-square plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordered sequence of sculptural elements at angles
rubrics_metrics.description: The angle decoration is arranged in the following manner: First, Three great bearing capitals (lower arcade). Secondly, Three figure subjects of sculpture above them (lower arcade). Thirdly, Three smaller bearing capitals (upper arcade). Fourthly, Three angels above them (upper arcade). Fifthly, Three spiral shafts with niches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an angle, verify the presence and order of these elements; consider how the sequence creates a cumulative vertical program from ground to parapet and whether each element performs its intended visual and symbolic role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of sculptural subject as declaration of purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: "If he has anything to say to us of the purpose with which he built the palace, it is sure to be said here; if there was any lesson which he wished principally to teach... this is the place in which we may be secure of finding it legibly inscribed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret subject matter (biblical scenes, judgments, moral themes) at principal corners as deliberate civic or ideological statements. Judge appropriateness and clarity of subject choice relative to public function of the building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contrasting sculptural programs to express temper of schools
rubrics_metrics.description: "The principal element in the Renaissance spirit, is its firm confidence in its own wisdom... the most characteristic sentiment... of the Gothic heart, was the frank confession of its own weakness." (illustrated by Fall of Man, Drunkenness of Noah, Judgment of Solomon)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate programs for whether subject selection and treatment embody broader stylistic/ideological temper (Gothic humility vs Renaissance confidence). Use comparative reading of corner subjects (e.g., Fall of Man vs Judgment of Solomon) to diagnose epochal intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angles as loci for the most important evidence of feeling and skill
rubrics_metrics.description: "These...are the very corner stones of the edifice, and in them we may expect to find the most important evidences of the feeling, as well as of the skill, of the builder."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize close study of corner sculpture when assessing the architect's and sculptor's intentions, aesthetic priorities, and technical competence. Look for thematic prominence and craftsmanship here first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of subject to architecture (tree as necessary adjunct)
rubrics_metrics.description: In both the subjects, of the Fall and the Drunkenness, the tree, which forms the chiefly decorative portion of the sculpture, — fig in the one case, vine in the other, — was a necessary adjunct. Its trunk... forms the true outer angle of the palace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether decorative elements (trees, vines) are functionally integrated into the architecture (e.g., serving as terminal forms at the angle) rather than being merely applied ornament. Favor designs where motif and structure cohere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic leafage and attention to botanical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nothing can be more masterly or superb than the sweep of this foliage... the broad leaves lapping round the budding fruit... carved every rib and vein upon them, in relief..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess level of naturalism in vegetal carving: undercutting, leaf veins, tendrils, placement of birds, and distribution of leaves. High-quality work will show detailed undercutting and botanical observation; note whether such detail enhances overall composition or becomes fragile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between vegetal workmanship and figure-work
rubrics_metrics.description: "As must always be the case in early sculpture, the figures are much inferior to the leafage; yet so skilful in many respects, that..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate relative skill exhibited in foliage versus human figures. In some periods/workshops, sculptors excelled in vegetation and were weaker in figure modelling; determine whether this imbalance serves architectural function (figures 'fitted for their architectural service') or undermines narrative clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability vs over-delicacy (risk of breakage)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The natural delicacy of the vine-leaf and tendril having tempted the sculptor to greater effort, he has passed the proper limits of his art, and cut the upper stems so delicately that half of them have been broken away by the casualties to which the situation of the sculpture necessarily exposes it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging technique, weigh aesthetic refinement against long-term durability. Excessive fineness in exposed external work risks loss; good practice respects material limits and site exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of undercutting and mass to preserve sculptural robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Notwithstanding the depth of the undercutting, the work remains nearly uninjured..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how undercutting and substantial massing were applied to achieve visual depth while preserving structural integrity. Successful carving maintains deep modelling without compromising resistance to weather and mechanical damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic features as dating evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The feet are protected simply by a bandage... a feature of dress which will be found in nearly every piece of figure sculpture in Venice, from the year 1300 to 1380... (used to date groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recurring costume and stylistic markers (foot bandages, hair/beard treatment, figure stiffness) to help date works; cross-reference with dated monuments and inscriptions for confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading historical layers: different epochs visible in sculptural program
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is impossible to overstate... the palace had been built at various epochs, and preserved... for the sole purpose of teaching us the difference in the temper of the two schools."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a façade reveals multiple historical phases; interpret juxtaposed styles as an intentional palimpsest that communicates changes in taste, politics, or ideology. Note how later additions dialogue with earlier work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation vs rebuilding: weighing repair against replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate after fires whether the ruin should be thrown down, and an entirely new palace built... the best architects... pleaded for the Gothic pile, and prevailed. It was successfully repaired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating conservation decisions, consider contemporary expert opinions, structural safety, cultural value of original fabric, and the merits of repair over wholesale replacement. Use documented advice and comparative analysis to justify approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive placement: corner sculpture as civic inscription
rubrics_metrics.description: "If there was any sentiment which they themselves desired to have expressed in the principal edifice of their city, this is the place in which we may be secure of finding it legibly inscribed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret major corner sculptures as civic or institutional inscriptions—read them for intended moral, religious, or political messaging. Evaluate legibility and effectiveness in communicating to contemporary viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptor's technical specialization revealed by comparative workmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The sculptor being evidently more practised in keen and fine lines of vegetation than in those of the figure; so that... he has failed in telling his story plainly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs that workshop strengths influenced outcomes (excellent foliage but weaker narrative figures). Judge whether technical specialization compromises or complements the program, and whether narrative clarity remains sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural proportion and emphasis given by plan shape
rubrics_metrics.description: "As the building was very nearly square on the ground plan, a peculiar prominence and importance were given to its angles, which rendered it necessary that they should be enriched and softened by sculpture."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ground-plan geometry when assessing decorative strategy: near-square plans increase importance of corners and justify concentrated ornament; evaluate whether ornament responds appropriately to plan-derived visual needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of inscriptions/tablets as documentary and decorative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The tablets bearing this important inscription have been taken out and reinserted... "Hoc opus illustris Michael Dux Stellifer auxit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess inscriptions for their documentary value (dates, patron names, claims of contribution) and for how they function compositely with ornament. Check authenticity and whether re-insertion or relocation has altered interpretive context.
